description: An evergreen oak with a dense, dark green, rounded crown, often several trunks, and small shiny leaves that are smooth-edged or spiny like holly; 8-15 m tall here. It grows on steeper, moister slopes and along ravines through the blue oak woodland and up into the lower conifer forest, and California scrub-jays bury its acorns, planting new oaks with the ones they never come back for.

season_notes.winter: Evergreen: still in full dark leaf, the green that picks it out among the bare blue oaks.
season_notes.spring: New pale leaves and catkins (March-May); the flowers become acorns that take two years to ripen.
season_notes.summer: A dense crown casting the deepest shade in the woodland; last year's flowers are now small green acorns.
season_notes.fall: Acorns that began in the spring of last year ripen and drop (September-November).

notes: Evergreen oak of foothill woodland, canyons and chaparral edges; a tree 8-22 m or a shrub on poor sites. Here 8-15 m. Often several trunks from the base or a low fork (stems 1-2, split_prob 0.5), short bole, dense rounded dark crown that hides most of the wood, so mid LOD draws only four limbs. Rauh's model with a decurrent crown like blue oak but denser (more level-1 and level-2 branches, higher foliage density). Bark smooth grey when young, darker grey and furrowed with age. Leaves 2.5-5 cm, oblong to lanceolate, flat (not cupped like coast live oak), entire or spiny-toothed, glossy dark green on both faces; new growth in spring is lighter. No seasonal leaf drop to speak of (leaves live about two years), so leaf_on is 1 all year.
